## 1. Introduction > How to use this guidance > Data and AI Ethics Self-Assessment Tool
Source: Data and AI Ethics Framework (`data-ethics`), Central Digital and Data Office. Authority: advisory. page last updated 2025-12-18.
Cite inline as: ([Data and AI Ethics Framework: Data and AI Ethics Self-Assessment Tool](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/data-ethics-framework/data-and-ai-ethics-framework#data-and-ai-ethics-self-assessment-tool))

Obligations in this section (verbatim, strength from the modal verb):
- [RECOMMENDED] "If your team is working on an AI or data-driven technology project, then as well as reading this guidance you should use the Data and AI Ethics Self-Assessment Tool."

Section text (verbatim):
> If your team is working on an AI or data-driven technology project, then as well as reading this guidance you should use the Data and AI Ethics Self-Assessment Tool.
> The tool will help you capture information, and share learnings, challenges and progress with colleagues. We recommend that you maintain it along with your other project documentation to record decision making across the life cycle of a project.

## 2. 7. Data management > 7.3 Data frameworks and operating models
Source: Government Functional Standard GovS 005: Digital (`govs-005`), Government Digital Service. Authority: mandatory. page last updated 2026-10-01.
Cite inline as: ([Government Functional Standard GovS 005: Digital: 7.3 Data frameworks and operating models](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/government-functional-standard-govs-005-digital/government-functional-standard-govs-005-digital-html#data-frameworks-and-operating-models))

Obligations in this section (verbatim, strength from the modal verb):
- [MANDATORY] "Organisations shall follow appropriate guidance when implementing data frameworks and operating models, including for cross-government data sharing, business intelligence, artificial intelligence, machine learning, automation and advanced analytics."
  - Possible conflict (machine-suggested, NOT verified): similar wording in "Service Manual", pages about 5.3 years apart: "Organisations should have COVID-19 operating guidelines to minimise the risk to researchers." https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/user-research/doing-user-research-during-coronavirus-covid-19-choosing-face-to-face-or-remote-research#protecting-researchers
  - Possible conflict (machine-suggested, NOT verified): similar wording in "The Rose Book: guidance on knowledge asset management in government", pages about 2.5 years apart: "Organisations must comply with the law governing personal data and ensure data is treated safely, securely and ethically within appropriate governance frameworks." https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/knowledge-asset-management-in-government/knowledge-asset-management-strategies-what-to-include-and-where-to-start#data-collection

Section text (verbatim):
> Organisations shall follow appropriate guidance when implementing data frameworks and operating models, including for cross-government data sharing, business intelligence, artificial intelligence, machine learning, automation and advanced analytics.
> Note: The following products provide best practice guidance:
> Principles for securing personal data in government services [footnote 24]
> AI Playbook for UK Government [footnote 25]
> Data and AI Ethics Framework [footnote 21]
> The Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard [footnote 26]

## 3. Buying AI > Aligning procurement and ethics
Source: AI Playbook for the UK Government (`ai-playbook`), Department for Science, Innovation and Technology. Authority: advisory. page last updated 2025-02-10, over a year ago.
Cite inline as: ([AI Playbook for the UK Government: Aligning procurement and ethics](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ai-playbook-for-the-uk-government/artificial-intelligence-playbook-for-the-uk-government-html#aligning-procurement-and-ethics))

Section text (verbatim):
> It’s important to consider and factor data ethics into your commercial approach from the outset.
> There’s a range of guidance relating to AI and data ethics to support public servants working with data and/or AI. This guidance collates existing ethical principles, developed by government and public sector bodies. You can also refer to the:
> Data ethics framework: this outlines appropriate and responsible data use in government and the wider public sector. The framework helps public servants understand ethical considerations, address these within their projects, and encourages responsible innovation
> Data ethics requirements checklist (PDF, 62.7KB) for suppliers: this will mitigate bias. It will also ensure diversity in development teams, transparency and interpretability, and explainability of the results
> Public Sector Contract (PSC): this includes provisions related to intellectual property rights, data protection, and equality, diversity and human rights

## 4. Introduction
Source: Data and AI Ethics Framework (`data-ethics`), Central Digital and Data Office. Authority: advisory. page last updated 2025-12-18.
Cite inline as: ([Data and AI Ethics Framework: Introduction](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/data-ethics-framework/data-and-ai-ethics-framework#introduction))

Section text (verbatim):
> This framework provides a set of principles and activities to guide the responsible development, procurement and use of data and artificial intelligence (AI) in the public sector. It helps public servants understand ethical considerations and how to address these in their work.
> Data and AI ethics is about using data and data-driven technologies responsibly, including:
> respecting privacy
> promoting fairness
> protecting individuals, communities and society from harm
> This includes ensuring that data is collected, shared and used in appropriate, fair, safe, sustainable and transparent ways.
> The framework applies to any project that involves:
> data (collection, sharing or use)
> data-driven technologies
> AI
> automated decision-making and algorithmic tools
> In this guidance, this is what we mean when we refer to ‘data and AI’.

## 5. (untitled)
Source: Data and AI Ethics Framework (`data-ethics`), Central Digital and Data Office. Authority: advisory. page last updated 2025-12-18.
Cite inline as: ([Data and AI Ethics Framework: (untitled)](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/data-ethics-framework))

Obligations in this section (verbatim, strength from the modal verb):
- [RECOMMENDED] "Any team working on an AI or data-driven technology project should also use the Data and AI Ethics Self-Assessment Tool."

Section text (verbatim):
> The Data and AI Ethics Framework sets out principles and activities to guide the responsible development, procurement and use of data and AI in the public sector.
> The framework is mainly written for people who work in government and other public sector organisations. For example, people who are designing, building, maintaining, using or updating projects that use data and AI. It will help public servants understand ethical considerations and how to address these in their work.
> Any team working on an AI or data-driven technology project should also use the Data and AI Ethics Self-Assessment Tool. The tool will help teams capture information, and share learnings, challenges and progress with colleagues.
